citeAs: Merity, S., Xiong, C., Bradbury, J., & Socher, R. (2016). Pointer Sentinel Mixture Models. arXiv:1609.07843.
creator: Stephen Merity, Caiming Xiong, James Bradbury, Richard Socher (MetaMind - A Salesforce Company)
description: WikiText is a language modeling benchmark dataset constructed from Wikipedia Good and Featured articles, available in two sizes: WikiText-2 (roughly twice the size of Penn Treebank) and WikiText-103 (over 103 million words). Unlike Penn Treebank, it retains original casing, punctuation, and a larger vocabulary, enabling evaluation of long-range dependencies and rare word prediction. The document-level version preserves article structure.
name: WikiText
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is sourced exclusively from Wikipedia Good and Featured articles, which are curated by Wikipedia editors and may not represent the full diversity of language use. The paper notes that other large-scale datasets either have restrictive licensing or randomized sentence ordering, motivating this Wikipedia-based approach.
rai:dataCollection: Articles were selected from Wikipedia that met the Good or Featured article criteria specified by Wikipedia editors. The text for each article was extracted using the Wikipedia API. This resulted in 23,805 Good articles and 4,790 Featured articles.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw Wikipedia article text extracted via the Wikipedia API from Good and Featured articles, including Wikipedia mark-up with macros for metric conversion, abbreviations, language notation, and date handling.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Sections primarily featuring lists were removed. Minor bugs such as sort keys and Edit buttons leaked from HTML were removed. Mathematical formulae and LaTeX code were replaced with <formula> tokens. Normalization and tokenization were performed using the Moses tokenizer, augmented to further split numbers (e.g., 8,600 → 8 @,@ 600). A vocabulary was constructed by discarding all words with a count below 3; words outside the vocabulary were mapped to the <unk> token.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to be freely available to the research community, addressing the lack of freely available large-scale language modeling benchmarks that allow for learning long-range dependencies.
rai:dataUseCases: Benchmark for word-level language modeling, particularly for evaluating models on longer-range dependencies, rare word prediction, and more realistic vocabularies than Penn Treebank. Intended to replace PTB as the standard language modeling benchmark.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Moses tokenizer (Koehn et al., 2007), augmented to further split numbers, used for normalization and tokenization of the raw Wikipedia text.

evidence.name: we also introduce a new benchmark dataset for language modeling called WikiText.
evidence.description: The dataset is available in two different sizes: WikiText-2 and WikiText-103. Both feature punctuation, original casing, a larger vocabulary, and numbers. WikiText-2 is two times the size of the Penn Treebank dataset. WikiText-103 features all extracted articles.

evidence.isLiveDataset: The dataset is available in two different sizes: WikiText-2 and WikiText-103. Both feature punctuation, original casing, a larger vocabulary, and numbers.
evidence.rai:dataCollection: We selected articles only fitting the Good or Featured article criteria specified by editors on Wikipedia. These articles have been reviewed by humans and are considered well written, factually accurate, broad in coverage, neutral in point of view, and stable. This resulted in 23,805 Good articles and 4,790 Featured articles. The text for each article was extracted using the Wikipedia API.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionType: The text for each article was extracted using the Wikipedia API. Extracting the raw text from Wikipedia mark-up is nontrivial due to the large number of macros in use.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The text for each article was extracted using the Wikipedia API. Extracting the raw text from Wikipedia mark-up is nontrivial due to the large number of macros in use. These macros are used extensively and include metric conversion, abbreviations, language notation, and date handling.
evidence.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Once extracted, specific sections which primarily featured lists were removed by default. Other minor bugs, such as sort keys and Edit buttons that leaked in from the HTML, were also removed. Mathematical formulae and LATEX code, were replaced with hformulai tokens. Normalization and tokenization were performed using the Moses tokenizer (Koehn et al., 2007), slightly augmented to further split numbers (8,600 → 8 @,@ 600) and with some additional minor fixes. evidence.rai:dataUseCases: We hope this new dataset can serve as a platform to improve handling of rare words and the usage of long term dependencies in language modeling.
evidence.rai:dataLimitations: WikiText-2 is two times the size of the Penn Treebank dataset. WikiText-103 features all extracted articles. Both datasets use the same articles for validation and testing with the only difference being the vocabularies.
evidence.rai:dataBiases: Unfortunately, they either have restrictive licensing which prevents widespread use or have randomized sentence ordering (Chelba et al., 2013) which is unrealistic for most language use and prevents the effective learning and evaluation of longer term dependencies. Hence, we constructed a language modeling dataset using text extracted from Wikipedia and will make this available to the community.
evidence.rai:dataSocialImpact: Since this commonly used dataset is small and no other freely available alternative exists that allows for learning long range dependencies, we also introduce a new benchmark dataset for language modeling called WikiText.
evidence.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Normalization and tokenization were performed using the Moses tokenizer (Koehn et al., 2007), slightly augmented to further split numbers (8,600 → 8 @,@ 600) and with some additional minor fixes.
evidence.license: we also introduce the freely available WikiText corpus.
